answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a graded deposit each identity must freeze before it can vote. When an operator splits one stake across a thousand puppets, every clone still posts its own separate bond, and a blank history caps it at the lowest tier, a ceiling creeping upward like a glacier. Climbing takes slow reputation, like water carving a canyon grain by grain. Clones therefore cost the attacker linearly in locked capital, and each fake vote carries only a sliver of weight. Through the prism of the ledger, a thousand linked clones resolve into one visible shape.
